verdict.rationale: Devin's docs describe exactly this workflow — delegating a plain-language ask (e.g., a Linear/Jira ticket or Slack mention) into an autonomous session that plans and implements a fix, with a draft you can take over in its IDE, which matches intent-to-spec conversion (devin-docs-1, devin-docs-4, devin-docs-5, devin-docs-23). However, independent early hands-on evidence found real gaps between plain-language asks and correctly scoped/executed tasks (e.g., only 13.8% of issues resolved, demo not matching the actual job requirements), suggesting the scoping/execution is inconsistent in practice. Missing for 10: recent independent benchmarks on scoping accuracy, first-party documentation of how task scope/plan is surfaced to the user before execution, and resolution of the community-reported failure cases.
